title: God Struct Monoliths (Large Class)
damaged_code:
```rust
struct SystemManager {
    db_conn: DbConnection,
    smtp_client: SmtpClient,
    active_users: Vec<User>,
    cache: Cache,
    config: Config,
    log_file: File,
    // Contains 30+ separate business functions acting on different fields
}
```
pattern: A massive struct aggregating dozens of unrelated fields and responsibilities, acting as the centralized coordinator for the entire application.
why_bad: Fails the Common Closure Principle and SRP. Any change to logging, database schemas, cache invalidation, or config formatting forces a rewrite and redeployment of the entire `SystemManager`. It creates a massive convergence of dependencies, making compile-time parallelization impossible.
detection: Measure structs containing numerous fields from disparate architectural layers (DB, Network, Log, Business Entities) combined with dozens of public methods.
counterexample: `Context-dependent`. Centralized application states in small CLI tools or tiny prototypes where simplicity outweighs separation of concerns.
source: *Robert C. Martin - Clean Code (2008)*, Chapter 10, "Classes" (Too Many Responsibilities); *Steve McConnell - Code Complete (2004)*, Chapter 6; *Martin Fowler - Refactoring (1999)*, Chapter 3, "Large Class".
